Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that water in the lake, which straddles the border between China's Tibet region and Nepal at the confluence of two rivers, has been slowly flowing out and gradually reducing the reservoir, state broadcaster CCTV reported, citing the Water Resources Ministry. By Saturday afternoon, parts of the lake bed had become visible, CCTV reported. The ministry said satellite imagery of the lake on the Purepu Tsangpo river showed it covered 99,000 square metres (1.1 million square feet) early on Saturday, roughly the size of 14 soccer pitches, having shrunk by 21,000 square metres since Thursday. A glacier collapse on Wednesday sent a torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris through Himalayan river systems, sweeping away a border port complex linking Tibet with Nepal, killing hundreds and leaving thousands missing. RISKS UNDER WATCH Experts and authorities have warned of an extremely high risk of secondary disasters in the valley, particularly from the lake formed by glacier debris, which could threaten rescue operations downstream. With water draining naturally, Water Resources Ministry experts said search and rescue operations downstream could continue safely if outflows remain low or manageable and recede completely within two to three days. Rescue workers could be notified promptly to evacuate if any abnormalities appear at the lake, with warnings issued more than 30 minutes in advance, CCTV cited the experts as saying. State-owned engineering and rescue company China Anneng, which has been monitoring the lake since Thursday, has deployed radar and drones around the lake for 24-hour surveillance, CCTV said. Initial [USN:L6N44P07I TEXT:"overflow"] from the lake on Friday temporarily halted rescue work before a subsequent assessment deemed the risks manageable. Authorities have also flagged another, larger body of water at the foot of the glacier collapse. "We estimate its area to be over 120,000 square metres, but its depth is currently unknown," said Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at the Ministry of Natural Resources' Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center. Flood risks will [USN:L6N44P0OC TEXT:"remain"] until both lakes have fully drained, an official with Nepal's Disaster Management Authority has said. LOOKING FOR SURVIVORS In bleak, rainy conditions on Saturday morning, more than 50 rescue workers combed through rubble of boulders and mud, looking for signs of life and calling out for survivors, CCTV reported. The first rescue team and a search dog reached the Gyirong border crossing complex on Friday afternoon and found it [USN:L6N44P04B TEXT:"reduced to ruins"]. Dangerous conditions at the main disaster zone, compounded by damaged roads and disrupted communications, continue to hamper Chinese relief efforts, state news agency Xinhua said. Forecasts show intermittent rain in the area over the next three days. Authorities are racing to reopen a key highway leading to the border port. By Saturday afternoon, crews had advanced within about 1.5 km (0.93 mile) of the site. China's death toll rose to seven early on Saturday, with 554 people still missing. Nearly 500 villagers and construction workers, along with 555 tourists in the area, have been evacuated, Xinhua said. CAUSE STILL UNCLEAR The cause of the collapse remains unclear, but climate experts say global warming could be a factor. "We're still not absolutely sure whether it was triggered by an earthquake or ... by warm temperatures melting the glacier," said Benjamin Horton, dean of the School of Energy and Environment at the City University of Hong Kong. Videos shared on social media and verified by Reuters show the lower section of the glacier near the Langtang Lirung mountain peak breaking away and plunging into the valley below, triggering an avalanche of ice and rock and a massive landslide. "One of the reasons why we don't fully understand the mechanisms that cause the landslide is that we have a lack of data. So there has to be this investment in the science, there has to be this investment in society," Horton said.

item.title: First-pitch homer, 2 other long balls send Diamondbacks past Giants
item.description: Lars Nootbaar hit the first pitch of the game for a home run, Corbin Carroll and Tim Tawa homered in a five-run third inning, and the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks overpowered the San Francisco Giants 10-6 on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lars Nootbaar hit the first pitch of the game for a home run, Corbin Carroll and Tim Tawa homered in a five-run third inning, and the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks overpowered the San Francisco Giants 10-6 on Friday. Nootbaar collected three hits for the Diamondbacks, who took advantage of a San Diego Padres loss earlier in the evening to move within a half-game of the National League's third and final wild-card spot. Bryce Eldridge and Christian Koss launched homers for the Giants -- the first of the season for Koss -- but the hosts were out-hit 12-5 en route to their ninth loss in 11 meetings with the Diamondbacks this season. The homers by Nootbaar, his fifth, Carroll, his 19th, and Tawa, his ninth, helped Arizona overcome Giants scoring in each of the first four innings. The Diamondbacks held a 6-5 lead entering the sixth inning, when they took charge with a three-run uprising featuring a two-RBI single by Ildemaro Vargas and Carroll's sacrifice fly for his third RBI of the night. Arizona relievers Gerardo Carrillo, Jonathan Loaisiga, Brandyn Garcia, Dennis Santana and Juan Morillo combined for five innings, permitting just one run, which was unearned, and one hit. Left-hander Kohl Drake, promoted from the minors earlier in the day, was pulled after four innings, having allowed four hits and five runs. He walked one and struck out four. Carrillo (3-1), who pitched a scoreless fifth inning to retain a one-run lead, was credited with the win. Giants starter Blade Tidwell (0-1) went five innings, allowing six runs on seven hits. He struck out four and walked one. The homer by Tawa, a three-run shot, came two pitches after Giants manager Tony Vitello was ejected for disputing Nolan Arenado's grounder over third base having been ruled fair. Arenado's double put runners on second and third in what then was a 3-2 game. Vitello was tossed for the second time in three days. Giants ace Logan Webb, watching from the dugout, also was ejected. Tawa, Arenado and James McCann had two hits apiece for Arizona, which earned a third win in four games. The homer by Eldridge was his 15th of the season. He finished with two hits and Jung Hoo Lee scored twice for the Giants, who had won three of four to open a seven-game homestand. --Field Level Media

item.title: Temasek backs Singapore Airlines' Air India investment amid growing scrutiny
item.description: Singapore state investor Temasek, the majority shareholder of Singapore Airlines , on Saturday backed the airline's investment in Air India, as scrutiny grows over its stake in the loss-making Indian carrier.
item.dc:creator: Abhijith Ganapavaram, Arpan Chaturvedi
item.content:encoded: Singapore state investor Temasek, the majority shareholder of Singapore Airlines (SIAL.SI) , on Saturday backed the airline's investment in Air India, as scrutiny grows over its stake in the loss-making Indian carrier. Air India's request for about $1.5 billion in fresh equity from owners Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines was first [USN:L1N44M0M1 TEXT:"reported by Reuters"] this week. Singapore Airlines owns 25.1% of India's second-largest airline, with the rest owned by Tata. News of the funding request prompted Kenneth Tiong, a lawmaker from Singapore's opposition Workers' Party, to urge that Temasek's funds [USN:L4N44O0J9 TEXT:"not to be used"] to shore up the Indian carrier. Singapore's Business Times also ran a commentary arguing that Singapore Airlines could not realistically exit its Air India stake, with Tata the only plausible buyer. It questioned what its 25.1% holding offered beyond a board seat and a share of the losses, while saying the strategic logic of the investment still held. In a letter to the newspaper responding to that commentary, Juliet Teo, joint head of portfolio development at Temasek Singapore, said Temasek viewed Singapore Airlines' decision to invest in Air India from a long-term perspective and was supportive of it. The letter said the transformation of Air India involved complex, multi-year operational and integration challenges, with outcomes shaped by industry developments and external factors such as airspace disruptions, geopolitical developments and fuel price volatility. "Efforts of this scale take time and are not expected to be linear," it said. Temasek did not address whether it would support any capital contribution by Singapore Airlines to Air India. Air India's multibillion-dollar revamp has been under way since Tata took control of the former state-owned carrier in 2022. Air India has been hit by Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian carriers, [USN:L6N41I0NM TEXT:"disruptions"] from the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, and the fallout from a crash last year that killed 260 people. In the year to March, the airline and its budget unit Air India Express posted combined losses of $2.33 billion, weighing on Singapore Airlines' profits. Singapore Airlines said on Thursday its board would carefully consider any requests for additional capital from Air India, taking into consideration the group's other capital requirements and Air India's business strategy.

item.title: Le Népal a besoin d'au moins $4 mds après des crues dévastatrices
item.description: Le Népal a besoin de 4 à 5 milliards de dollars pour financer les efforts de reconstruction après les crues dévastatrices survenues mercredi dans la région himalayenne entre le Népal et le Tibet chinois, a dit samedi à Reuters le ministre népalais des Finances, Swarnim Wagle.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Sharma
item.content:encoded: Le Népal a besoin de 4 à 5 milliards de dollars pour financer les efforts de reconstruction après les [USN:L8N44P08L TEXT:"crues"] dévastatrices survenues mercredi dans la région himalayenne entre le Népal et le Tibet chinois, a dit samedi à Reuters le ministre népalais des Finances, Swarnim Wagle. "Il s'agit seulement d'une estimation. Les pertes et dégâts sont en cours d'évaluation", a-t-il indiqué, notant toutefois que les besoins sont moindres que lors du séisme de 2015. L'effondrement d'un glacier mercredi a provoqué un torrent de roches, de glace, de boue et de débris dans les cours d'eau de l'Himalaya, faisant plus de 600 morts au Népal et au Tibet. Plus de 2.000 personnes sont toujours portées disparues. Ces inondations ont rasé des villes près de la zone frontalière, emportant ponts et routes et endommageant d'importantes centrales hydroélectriques. Swarnim Wagle n'a pas précisé la raison pour laquelle le coût de la reconstruction pourrait être inférieur aux 9 milliards de dollars dépensés après le séisme de magnitude 7,8 survenu en 2015, la pire catastrophe jamais enregistrée au Népal. Ce séisme avait fait près de 9.000 morts, détruit plus d'un demi-million de logements et engendré des pertes estimées à environ un tiers de l'économie népalaise. Les récentes inondations devraient néanmoins constituer un coup dur pour une économie qui dépend des envois de fonds, du tourisme et de l'hydroélectricité car des centrales électriques représentant plus de 12% de la capacité de production nationale ont été détruites.

item.title: Edmundo Sosa's ninth-inning slam propels Phillies past Angels
item.description: Pinch hitter Edmundo Sosa hit a go-ahead grand slam with two outs in the top of the ninth inning as the Philadelphia Phillies rallied for a 5-3 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Friday night in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Edmundo Sosa hit a go-ahead grand slam with two outs in the top of the ninth inning as the Philadelphia Phillies rallied for a 5-3 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Friday night in Anaheim, Calif. Sosa drove a 1-1 changeup from Sammy Peralta 404 feet into the rock pile behind the fence in left-center for his sixth home run of the season and first career grand slam. Angels closer Ben Joyce (0-2) had loaded the bases in the inning by hitting Alec Bohm with a one-out pitch and walking Justin Crawford and J.T. Realmuto, the latter after right fielder Wade Meckler reached over the fence to rob Bryson Stott of a three-run go-ahead homer for the second out of the inning. Sosa was the first batter Peralta faced. Luis Arraez and Kyle Schwarber each had two hits and Bohm scored two runs for Philadelphia, which won for the 11th time in 13 games. Alex McFarlane (4-1) picked up the win with a scoreless inning of relief, and Jonathan Bowlan struck out Jose Siri and pinch hitter Adam Frazier with two men on in the bottom of the ninth to pick up his second save. Meckler went 1-for-3 with a walk, an RBI and a run for Los Angeles, which scored two runs on wild pitches during a three-run first inning. The Angels took their fifth straight loss. Los Angeles took advantage of Philadelphia starter Andrew Painter's wildness while building a 3-0 lead in the first inning. Zach Neto led off with a walk, advanced to second on a single by Mike Trout and then scored on a single to center by Meckler. Vaughn Grissom then sacrificed the runners along to second and third, a move that would pay big dividends as Trout and Meckler would later both score on wild pitches. Philadelphia cut the deficit to 3-1 in the fifth inning, snapping a 20-inning scoreless streak by Angels starter Reid Detmers. Bohm and Bryan De La Cruz opened the inning with back-to-back singles, and Bohm went to third on a flyout by Stott. One out later, Derek Hill drove in Bohm with a bunt single up the first base line. The Phillies had a chance to add on another run when Schwarber followed with a single to right. However, De La Cruz, who ran through a stop sign at third, hesitated between third and home and ended up getting thrown out easily at home by Josh Lowe to end the inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nepal's flood damage may cost up to a tenth of economy to rebuild
item.description: Nepal may need $4 billion to $5 billion to rebuild after this week's devastating floods, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters on Saturday, a bill equal to nearly a tenth of the economy.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Sharma
item.content:encoded: Nepal may need $4 billion to $5 billion to rebuild after this week's [USN:L6N44Q00H TEXT:"devastating floods,"] Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters on Saturday, a bill equal to nearly a tenth of the economy. "The initial estimate is between $4-$5 billion. Just an estimate," Wagle said. "We will require much less than what we needed for the 2015 earthquake. Loss and damage is being assessed." A glacier collapse on Wednesday unleashed a huge torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris through Himalayan mountain river systems, killing more than 600 people in Nepal and China's Tibet, with more than 2,000 still unaccounted for. The flood levelled towns in the border area, sweeping away bridges and roads and damaging major hydropower stations. Wagle did not elaborate on why the reconstruction bill was expected to be less than the $9 billion spent after the 2015 magnitude-7.8 quake, Nepal's worst recorded disaster. It killed nearly 9,000 people, destroyed more than half a million homes and caused losses estimated at around a third of Nepal's economy. Wednesday's floods will nevertheless be a major blow to an economy reliant on remittances, tourism and hydropower, damaging power projects that account for more than 12% of national generating capacity.

item.title: Le Népal a besoin d'aide dans les domaines techniques-ministre des AE
item.description: Le Népal a besoin d'une aide étrangère dans des domaines spécialisés et techniques où il ne dispose pas d'expertise après qu'un torrent de boue, de roches, de glace et de débris a dévasté il y a deux jours les vallées de l'Himalaya au Tibet et au Népal, a déclaré à Reuters le ministre népalais des Affaires étrangères, Shisir Khanal.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma
item.content:encoded: Le Népal a besoin d'une aide étrangère dans des domaines spécialisés et techniques où il ne dispose pas d'expertise après qu'un torrent de boue, de roches, de glace et de débris a dévasté il y a deux jours les vallées de l'Himalaya au Tibet et au Népal, a déclaré à Reuters le ministre népalais des Affaires étrangères, Shisir Khanal. L'effondrement d'un glacier a déclenché mercredi un torrent de roches, de glace, de boue et de débris qui s'est déversé dans les cours d'eau himalayens, faisant plus de 600 morts au Népal et au Tibet chinois, tandis que plus de 2.000 personnes sont toujours portées disparues. L'inondation a ravagé des zones proches de la frontière chinoise, rasant des villes entières et endommageant des centrales hydroélectriques. Le quotidien népalais Kathmandu Post a rapporté que l'Inde, la Chine, les Etats-Unis, la Grande-Bretagne, le Japon, la Corée du Sud, le Sri Lanka et le Bangladesh avaient demandé au gouvernement d'autoriser leurs équipes de recherche et de sauvetage à participer aux opérations. Shisir Khanal a déclaré que Katmandou avait besoin d'une aide étrangère dans des domaines tels que le sauvetage de personnes bloquées dans des tunnels, le rétablissement des transports et des communications dans les zones où des ponts ont été détruits, l'identification des corps, les tests ADN et la conservation des corps sur de longues périodes. "Nous avons déjà sollicité ces services spécialisés et cette assistance technique dans les domaines où nous ne disposons pas d'une expertise et d'un savoir-faire technique suffisants", a-t-il dit vendredi soir. Plus tôt dans la journée, le ministère népalais des Affaires étrangères avait déclaré que Katmandou pouvait pour l'instant gérer seul les opérations de sauvetage et avait refusé toute intervention étrangère. Interrogé sur cette position de son gouvernement, Shisir Khanal a déclaré qu'aucune aide n'était nécessaire pour les opérations générales de recherche et de sauvetage, qui étaient menées par les sauveteurs népalais. Les responsables des secours au Népal ont indiqué que de nombreux corps avaient été emportés par les eaux puis repêchés à environ 100 kilomètres de la zone frappée par le torrent. Les autorités népalaises ont indiqué que les inondations avaient causé d'importants dégâts aux bâtiments scolaires, aux hôpitaux, aux centrales hydroélectriques, aux routes, aux ponts et à d'autres infrastructures. Le Népal aura besoin de l'aide internationale pour les travaux de reconstruction et de réhabilitation à venir, ont-elles ajouté. Shisir Khanal a indiqué que, selon certaines informations, des personnes auraient pu se retrouver piégées à l'intérieur des tunnels des centrales hydroélectriques. Le Népal n'a que peu d'expérience en matière de tunnels et a besoin d'équipements ainsi que de savoir-faire technique pour mener à bien des opérations de sauvetage dans ces tunnels, a-t-il précisé.

item.title: Mertens joins Parry in Monterrey final after rallying past Bartunkova
item.description: Belgian second seed Elise Mertens recovered from a set down to beat Czech Nikola Bartunkova 1-6 6-4 6-2 at the Monterrey Open on Friday, setting up a final showdown with Diane Parry in the WTA 500 hardcourt tune-up event ahead of the U.S. Open.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Belgian second seed Elise Mertens recovered from a set down to beat Czech Nikola Bartunkova 1-6 6-4 6-2 at the Monterrey Open on Friday, setting up a final showdown with Diane Parry in the WTA 500 hardcourt tune-up event ahead of the U.S. Open. Frenchwoman Parry, 23, earlier upset American fifth seed Ann Li 7-6(7) 6-4 in two hours and three minutes in the first semi-final to book her place in the final. In the second semi-final, Bartunkova made a blistering start, breaking Mertens in the opening game before racing to a 4-1 lead. The 20-year-old secured a second break and never allowed Mertens a route back, closing out the set 6-1 after breaking serve for a third time in the final game. After being outplayed in the opening set, Mertens battled back in the second from a 3-0 deficit. The 30-year-old turned the tide by breaking in three consecutive return games and winning six of the final seven games to take the set 6-4 and draw level. Mertens carried that momentum into the decider, securing an early break for a 2-1 lead. She tightened her grip on the contest with another break in a marathon seventh game before serving out the set 6-2 to complete the comeback victory. The U.S. Open women's singles main draw begins on Sunday.

item.title: Louisiana judge opens door wider for return of pro hopefuls to SEC
item.description: The Southeastern Conference's attempt to stop athletes from returning from the pros to college rosters hit another roadblock Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Southeastern Conference's attempt to stop athletes from returning from the pros to college rosters hit another roadblock Friday. District Court Judge William Jorden of Baton Rouge, La., granted an amended temporary restraining order (TRO) that restored the eligibility of some athletes and blocked the SEC's plan to punish schools that recruit former pro hopefuls. Thirty-three athletes brought the Louisiana case, and the TRO now specifically names the SEC and its commissioner, Greg Sankey. Among those impacted, according to the (Baton Rouge) Advocate, are former New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Zxavian Harris and former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright, both of whom are committed to play this fall at LSU. Per the report, Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge defender Jack Pyburn also hopes to play for the Tigers if he is cut before the end of August. A hearing is scheduled before Jorden in Baton Rouge on Thursday, just over 48 hours before the Tigers kick off the season at home against Clemson. Tony Clayton, one of the plaintiffs' attorneys, said, according to ESPN, "If Sankey shows up, I'd like to hear his argument. What gives him the right to anoint himself God and take these constitutional rights from these kids?" The latest legal maneuvering comes a day after District Court Judge Martin Hoffman of Dallas ruled that the SEC cannot block a group of 41 athletes from returning to college despite their dalliances with pro leagues. The plaintiffs in the Dallas case include three active NFL players, wide receiver Omari Evans and linebacker Wesley Bissainthe, both Kansas City Chiefs, and Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Jordan Hudson, plus two players who signed WNBA contracts, Bailey Maupin and Christeen Iwuala. The SEC was joined this week by the Big Ten, Big 12 and Atlantic Coast Conference in announcing rules prohibiting athletes from returning to college. The SEC's new ban affects players who declared for a pro draft and did not withdraw, signed a pro contract or appeared on a pro team's roster. The SEC also reportedly voted 15-0 on Wednesday -- with LSU abstaining -- to allow the league to sanction schools and coaches that add former pro athletes to their rosters. According to multiple media reports, the SEC's penalties would include suspending coaches for half a season, imposing a fine equal to 50% of the sport's annual operating budget and revoking league voting rights. Clayton said, according to the Advocate, "The SEC and the NCAA have to follow the rules, just as the rest of us. They're not a communist nation." Both cases follow the NCAA's adoption of a new age-based eligibility model that allows athletes up to five seasons within a five-year eligibility period. Athletes who had exhausted their eligibility by the end of 2025-26 were excluded from the transition. --Field Level Media

item.title: NFL preseason roundup: Ravens rout Commanders to finish unbeaten
item.description: Tyler Huntley threw for a first-quarter touchdown to open the scoring, Joe Fagnano threw a TD pass and added a scoring run and the host Baltimore Ravens completed an unbeaten preseason by thrashing the Washington Commanders 41-3 on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tyler Huntley threw for a first-quarter touchdown to open the scoring, Joe Fagnano threw a TD pass and added a scoring run and the host Baltimore Ravens completed an unbeaten preseason by thrashing the Washington Commanders 41-3 on Friday night. Huntley's 25-yard touchdown pass to Chris Moore highlighted a 4-for-4 passing performance for 61 yards. Fagnano scored on a 1-yard run later in the opening quarter to give Baltimore a 14-0 advantage. Tyler Loop booted a 51-yard field goal in the second quarter before Fagnano connected with LaJohntay Wester for a 10-yard touchdown. Jonathan Ward added a 2-yard touchdown run in the third quarter and finished with 53 yards on seven carries for Baltimore. Washington got its only points on Drew Stevens' 39-yard field goal before Loop answered with a 24-yarder to make it 34-3. Falcons 17, Dolphins 12 In the final preseason tuneup before the team officially names a Week 1 quarterback starter, Tua Tagovailoa threw for 95 yards and lost a fumble for the visiting Falcons (2-1) in a 17-12 victory over Miami (0-3). Tagovailoa, who appears to be the likely starter with Michael Penix Jr. unable to appear in the preseason after suffering a partially torn ACL last November, completed 7 of 8 passes against his former team before being lifted for Cooper Rush. Tagovailoa hit Kyle Pitts Sr. for a 37-yard pass to highlight an opening drive that was stamped with Brian Robinson's 3-yard touchdown rush. Atlanta's second drive lasted one play as Tagovailoa lost a fumble on a botched snap. Miami's Cam Miller completed 7 of 16 passes for 71 yards and Mark Gronowski had 97 passing yards in relief. Former Falcon Riley Patterson's four field goals accounted for the entirety of the Dolphins' scoring. Panthers 16, Texans 13 In a game that saw both teams rest their starters, Miles Davis rushed for a touchdown and Ryan Fitzgerald made all three of his field goal attempts to lift Carolina to a victory over visiting Houston. Houston (0-3) committed three of its four turnovers in the first half. Backup quarterback Davis Mills was picked off by second-year safety Lathan Ransom, while journeyman Brett Rypien threw a touchdown, but lost a fumble and was intercepted by Cam Miller. Rypien got the majority of the run under center. He completed 13 of 23 passes for 101 yards and threw a 6-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to Zay Jones. Kyle Trask (19-for-28, 147 yards and an interception) and Kenny Pickett (5-for-8, 48 yards) split time at quarterback for Carolina (3-1). Pickett is considered to be the likely second-stringer to Bryce Young when the regular season begins. Giants 23, Jets 6 Jake Haener threw for a touchdown, Tyrone Tracy added another on the ground and the Giants stifled the Jets en route to an easy victory in each team's preseason finale. After stints by Jameis Winston (4-for-9, 54 yards and an interception) and Brandon Allen (8-for-12, 78 yards), Haener went 6-for-7 and found Xavier Gipson on a 37-yard touchdown. In one final audition for the role of Geno Smith's backup, none of the three Jets quarterbacks were overly impressive on Friday. Rookie Cade Klubnik threw for 59 yards and was picked off by Zaire Barnes, while Brady Cook threw for 26 yards and Bailey Zappe went 2-for-5 for 12 yards. Damon Bankston led all rushers with 62 yards for the Giants (2-1), while Chip Trayanum, who left with a neck injury, had 38 yards on the ground and a touchdown for the Jets (1-2). Jaguars 19, Buccaneers 0 Bryan Thomas Jr., T.J. Bollers and Amari Burney combined for five sacks as host Jacksonville harassed Tampa Bay in a shutout victory. Thomas racked up 2.5 sacks to go along with four quarterback hits and five tackles for the Jaguars (2-1). Carter Bradley had 77 passing yards and a touchdown toss to DeeJay Dallas. Michael Wortham scored on a 63-yard punt return, and Cam Little added a 61-yard field goal. The Buccaneers (2-1) gave a surprise start to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, but he found little success, surrendering a fumble and finishing 8 of 15 for 57 yards. Tampa Bay managed just 87 total yards and six first downs. Saints 27, Cowboys 24 Three New Orleans players scored rushing touchdowns and Daniel Carlson prevented a collapse with a 53-yard field goal as the Saints held off Dallas in Arlington, Texas. The Cowboys (2-1) rallied with 15 fourth-quarter points to tie the game at 24-all. Sam Howell directed the effort, completing 12 of 18 passes for 155 yards with two touchdowns. Jordan Hudson was his favorite target, notching four catches for 97 yards with a TD. Saints quarterback Zach Wilson directed an eight-play, 44-yard drive in response, resulting in Carlson's game-winner with 1:55 to play. Quarterback Spencer Rattler, wide receiver Barion Brown and running back Zamir White had the touchdowns for New Orleans (1-2). Packers 42, Cardinals 38 In a high-scoring preseason affair, host Green Bay got four touchdown passes from Kyle McCord, including two in the final four minutes, to nip Arizona and finish 2-1 in the preseason. McCord, a second-year player out of Syracuse, completed 22 of 35 passes for 226 yards and no interceptions. He connected with Kisean Johnson on a 28-yard scoring play with 3:19 left before directing a 44-yard scoring drive in the closing seconds. He and Johnson connected again from 10 yards out with 20 seconds left. The Cardinals (1-3) got touchdown passes from Kedon Slovis and Gardner Minshew. Evan Hull rumbled for 107 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries, while Simi Fehoko produced 94 yards and two touchdowns on five catches. Rivaldo Fairweather made eight receptions for 89 yards. Chiefs 9, Seahawks 9 An inauspicious preseason for two winless teams ended in a tie, as Seattle (0-2-1) missed a field-goal attempt at the gun to finish in a deadlock with host Kansas City. Jason Myers' 52-yard try with three seconds left missed wide right. Myers converted from 46 yards earlier in the contest but missed an extra-point kick. Second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe accounted for the Seahawks' other score, a third-quarter touchdown pass to Nick Vannett. The Chiefs (0-2-1) could manage only three short Harrison Butker field goals, though he also missed a third-quarter try from 58 yards. Brashard Smith ran for 72 yards on 16 carries. Bengals 30, Eagles 13 Visiting Cincinnati used two fourth-quarter touchdowns to finish off Philadelphia and wrap up a perfect preseason. Kentrel Bullock capped an 11-play, 77-yard drive with a 6-yard rushing score to give the Bengals (3-0) breathing room in the fourth, 23-13. Jamal Haynes followed with a 39-yard scoring scamper a little over a minute later. Josh Johnson directed the Bengals' offense with 156 yards through the air. Andy Dalton threw for 104 yards and a touchdown against his former team as he attempts to secure a roster spot with the Eagles (0-3). Running back Carson Steele had a touchdown catch among his eight receptions for 52 yards, and he added 24 yards on eight carries. Broncos 34, Vikings 6 Sam Ehlinger made the most of his preseason finale as he led Denver to a lopsided win over visiting Minnesota. Ehlinger completed 15 of 20 passes for 233 yards, three touchdowns and one interception for Denver (2-1). Running back Cody Schrader amassed 132 total yards (90 rushing, 42 receiving) and a touchdown. Max Brosmer completed 20 of 35 passes for 165 yards for Minnesota (1-2). Jermar Jefferson led the team with 59 rushing yards on six carries, and Dontae Fleming had a team-high 55 receiving yards on four catches. Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. left the game in the first quarter because of a foot injury. Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy did not play because of an ankle injury that he sustained a week ago against the Baltimore Ravens. McCarthy is competing for the backup role with veteran Carson Wentz, who completed 3 of 4 passes for 15 yards before giving way to Brosmer. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets rookie RB Chip Trayanum taken to hospital with neck injury
item.description: New York Jets rookie running back Chip Trayanum suffered a neck injury during the Jets' preseason game against the New York Giants Friday night in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Jets rookie running back Chip Trayanum suffered a neck injury during the Jets' preseason game against the New York Giants Friday night in East Rutherford, N.J. Trayanum was hit by Giants linebacker Trace Ford on the final play of the first half and remained down on the field motionless afterward. The undrafted rookie out of Toledo was immediately attended to by medical personnel before being carted off and transported to a local hospital. The Jets announced that he was awake, alert and moving his extremities en route to the hospital. Trayanum led all Jets rushers with 12 carries for 38 yards and a touchdown and added two receptions for 25 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: Colson Montgomery's homer sparks White Sox's victory over Twins
item.description: Colson Montgomery went 2-for-4 with a homer and three RBIs as the Chicago White Sox recorded a 7-4 win over the Minnesota Twins on Friday night in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Colson Montgomery went 2-for-4 with a homer and three RBIs as the Chicago White Sox recorded a 7-4 win over the Minnesota Twins on Friday night in Minneapolis. Andrew Benintendi finished 2-for-4 with a double and two RBIs for Chicago, which won its third straight game by taking the opener of a three-game series. Brooks Lee homered, singled and tallied three RBIs to lead Minnesota. Kody Clemens added a solo home run and a base hit, and top prospect Walker Jenkins singled and walked in his big-league debut. White Sox right-hander Grant Taylor (7-2) pitched 2 2/3 scoreless innings of relief. He allowed one hit, walked none and struck out three. Starter Luis Castillo allowed four runs on eight hits and a walk over four innings. Twins right-hander Dean Kremer (2-5) allowed six runs (five earned) on seven hits over four-plus innings. He walked three and struck out three. White Sox left-hander Bryan Hudson pitched a scoreless ninth for his sixth save. The White Sox opened the scoring with four runs in the top of the first. Benintendi ripped an RBI single to center to start the scoring. Two batters later, with runners on first and third and two outs, Montgomery stepped to the plate and belted a three-run homer to right field to make it 4-0. Minnesota responded with three runs in the bottom of the first. After Luke Keaschall hit a leadoff single, Lee socked a two-run homer to right-center field. Two batters later, Clemens hit a solo homer to right. The Twins evened the score at 4-all in the second. Trevor Larnach hit a leadoff double, advanced to third on a flyout and scored on Lee's two-out single. The White Sox reclaimed a 5-4 lead in the third. Benintendi doubled to left, driving in Munetaka Murakami, who had doubled. In the fourth, the White Sox increased their advantage to 6-4 when Tristan Peters scored on a passed ball by Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers. Another Twins miscue gave Chicago a 7-4 lead in the eighth. Right-hander Travis Adams threw a wild pitch in the dirt that bounced away from Jeffers, and Chase Meidroth took advantage by sprinting home from third base. --Field Level Media

item.title: China's CXMT to supply memory chip for Xiaomi's upcoming folding phone
item.description: China's top memory chipmaker, CXMT , will supply its latest LPDDR6 DRAM chips for Xiaomi's upcoming flagship folding phone, the companies said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's top memory chipmaker, CXMT (688825.SS) , will supply its latest LPDDR6 DRAM chips for Xiaomi's upcoming flagship folding phone, the companies said on Saturday. ChangXin Memory Technologies has started mass production of LPDDR6, which will supply Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi's new foldable phone 18 Fold, CXMT posted on China's Weibo social media platform. LPDDR6 arrived less than a year after CXMT mass-produced the previous generation of LPDDR5 chips. Xiaomi, one of the world's largest smartphone makers, confirmed the plan on its official Weibo account. The companies said the new foldable phone will be released in September. LPDDR6 is CXMT's most advanced Dynamic Random-Access Memory chip for mobile devices, narrowing the company's technology gap with China's top DRAM maker and global peers such as Samsung and SK Hynix. Xiaomi said this week the upcoming folding phone is expected to use a new version of the company's in-house 3-nanometre handset processor Xring O3, which would support LPDDR6. On Friday, CXMT posted a sharp [USN:L6N44P0PS TEXT:"turnaround to profit"] in the first half in its first earnings release since listing, while revenue spiked 874% from a year earlier to 150.3 billion yuan ($22.36 billion). The Hefei-based company said it had shipped to customers samples of its LPDDR6 DRAM chips, which are to be used on mobile devices, servers and smart cars - to customers. Also on Friday, CXMT [USN:L1N44Q004 TEXT:"sued the Pentagon"] over being placed on a list of companies the U.S. says are aiding China's military. The Pentagon declined to comment on ongoing litigation.

item.title: Quinn Mathews earns first major league win as Cardinals beat Pirates
item.description: Rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews pitched effectively into the sixth inning for his first major league victory and Jimmy Crooks hit a two-run homer for the St. Louis Cardinals, who beat the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates 4-1 on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews pitched effectively into the sixth inning for his first major league victory and Jimmy Crooks hit a two-run homer for the St. Louis Cardinals, who beat the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates 4-1 on Friday night. Jordan Walker added three hits and scored twice for the Cardinals, who had lost five of six coming in but remain fringe contenders in the National League wild-card hunt. St. Louis is 4 1/2 games behind the San Diego Padres for the final NL postseason spot. Mathews (1-2) allowed a run, five hits and a walk, striking out seven over 5 2/3 innings in his fourth career start. A consensus top-50 overall prospect in the preseason, Mathews was promoted from Triple-A for his debut Aug. 1. He had OK results in his first two appearances before being tagged for seven runs and 10 hits in five innings in his start against the Philadelphia Phillies on Aug. 22. After Nolan Gorman hit a one-out double and reached third base on an error by outfielder Oneil Cruz in the third, Crooks belted a 416-foot homer to right field against right-hander Jared Jones for a 2-0 lead. It was the fifth homer for Crooks, who came in batting .171 and had not gone deep since Aug. 3. Nathan Church added a sacrifice fly in the fourth for a 3-0 lead. Jones (2-6) allowed three runs, seven hits and a walk to go with six strikeouts over 4 1/3 innings. He dropped his fifth straight decision. Jared Triolo lined an RBI single in the fifth to bring the Pirates within 3-1, and they had runners at second and third with two outs before Esmerlyn Valdez struck out. The Cardinals caught a break when the Pirates tried to rally with two outs in the eighth. St. Louis right-hander Ryan Fernandez had retired the first six batters he faced in relief, but he walked Bryan Reynolds and the Cardinals brought in left-hander Caleb Ferguson to face Cruz. Cruz hit a liner about 105 mph, but the ball hit Reynolds in the leg on the way to right field for the third out. Cruz was credited with a single, but the inning was over. The Pirates' third error of the game, on a wild throw by shortstop Jacob Gonzalez, allowed Walker to score an insurance run in the bottom of the eighth. With closer Riley O'Brien unavailable, right-hander Ryne Stanek pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his second save. The Pirates, who are 10-15 in August, have scored a total of five runs in the past five games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Campeón Cruz Azul rompe racha de derrotas con goleada visitante en torneo mexicano
item.description: Cruz Azul, vigente campeón del fútbol mexicano, puso fin a una racha de tres derrotas consecutivas al golear el viernes por 3-1 como visitante a Necaxa en el inicio de la sexta jornada del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cruz Azul, vigente campeón del fútbol mexicano, puso fin a una racha de tres derrotas consecutivas al golear el viernes por 3-1 como visitante a Necaxa en el inicio de la sexta jornada del torneo Apertura. La "Máquina Celeste" de Cruz Azul, que no ganaba desde el 21 de julio, obtuvo el ansiado triunfo gracias a los goles de Jeremy Márquez, del argentino Nicolás Ibáñez y del colombiano Willer Ditta. En el partido disputado en el estadio Victoria de Aguascalientes, Cruz Azul se adelantó a los 23 minutos cuando Márquez remató de volea un tiro de esquina enviado por Carlos Rodríguez desde el sector izquierdo, metiendo el balón pegado al poste derecho. Ibáñez anotó el segundo gol a los 46 minutos con un colocado disparo desde fuera del área tras recibir pase de Rodríguez. El tercer gol cayó a los 53 minutos por conducto de Ditta, quien definió de derecha dentro del área tras hacer jugada de pared con el argentino José Antonio Paradela. Necaxa descontó a los 83 minutos con un disparo de Emilio Rodríguez desde fuera del área, metiendo el balón junto al poste izquierdo. En los otros partidos del viernes, Tijuana venció por 2-0 a Pumas UNAM con dos penales que anotó Gilberto Mora En tanto, Atlante y León empataron 1-1 con goles del argentino Martin Sarrafiore y José Alfonso Alvarado, respectivamente. El sábado se jugarán los encuentros entre Atlas-Querétaro, Pachuca-Guadalajara, América-Puebla y Santos Laguna-Tigres UANL. La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Toluca juegue ante Bravos de Ciudad Juárez y Monterrey enfrente al Atlético de San Luis.

item.title: Référendum en Islande sur les négociations d'adhésion à l'UE
item.description: L'Islande se prononce samedi sur une réouverture des négociations d'adhésion à l'Union européenne (UE) lors d'un référendum qui s'annonce très serré.
item.dc:creator: Tom Little, Johan Ahlander
item.content:encoded: L'Islande se prononce samedi sur une réouverture des négociations d'adhésion à l'Union européenne (UE) lors d'un référendum qui s'annonce très serré. Les électeurs islandais sont partagés à parts égales entre les partisans de l'ouverture de ces négociations et ceux qui estiment que l'Islande doit rester hors de l'UE. Un sondage publié vendredi par Gallup a montré qu'une courte majorité d'électeurs était opposé à la reprise des négociations. D'autres sondages réalisés récemment faisaient ressortir une courte majorité en faveur des négociations. Les partisans du "oui" estiment que rejoindre l'UE pourrait mener à une baisse des taux d'intérêt et offrir davantage de sécurité au pays dans un monde déstabilisé par la guerre en Ukraine ou les menaces du président américain Donald Trump d'acquérir le Groenland. Pour les partisans du "non", rejoindre le bloc menacerait la souveraineté de l'Islande et le secteur de la pêche, essentiel à l'économie de l'île. Le scrutin du 29 août ne porte pas sur l'adhésion en soi et si la réponse à une reprise des pourparlers avec l'UE est positive, cela obligerait l'Islande à organiser un second référendum sur l'adhésion à l'Union européenne. QUESTIONS ANCIENNES, URGENCE NOUVELLE "Je pense que l'Islande ferait mieux de ne pas adhérer à l'UE", a dit jeudi l'ancienne Première ministre Katrin Jakobsdottir aux journalistes après un évènement de campagne des opposants au projet organisé à Reykjavik, la capitale islandaise. "Pour un pays comme le nôtre, avec notre petite économie, il est très important de conserver notre souveraineté et de ne pas transférer davantage de pouvoir que nécessaire à l'UE." L'Islande a déposé sa candidature à l'UE en 2009, après l'effondrement de son système bancaire l'année précédente. Quatre années de négociations plus tard, un gouvernement eurosceptique a suspendu le processus en 2013. Les nouvelles tensions géopolitiques ont entraîné une urgence nouvelle sur une question dont les Islandais débattent par intermittence depuis des décennies. La ministre des Affaires étrangères, Thorgerdhur Katrin Gunnarsdottir, partisane du "oui", a déclaré la semaine dernière à Reuters que le scrutin de samedi pouvait se résumer à une simple question: L'Islande peut-elle se permettre de rester isolée dans un monde ou les anciennes certitudes s'écroulent? "L'ordre international qui sous-tendait pendant des décennies notre sécurité et notre prospérité subit d'importantes pressions", a-t-elle affirmé. "Dans un moment comme celui-ci, les petits pays doivent réfléchir attentivement à l'endroit où ils se tiennent, et qui se tient à leurs côtés." TAUX D'INTÉRÊT ET COÛT DE LA VIE En Islande, les débats se sont davantage concentrés sur les questions des taux d'intérêt, des droits de pêche et du coût de la vie que sur celle de la sécurité. L'Islande est aux prises avec une inflation élevée et persistante, et à une hausse des taux d'intérêt qui s'avère punitive pour les emprunteurs. Les partisans du "oui" disent que rejoindre l'UE et, peut-être, adopter l'euro pourrait apporter un certain soulagement. Le taux directeur de la banque centrale islandaise est de 8,0%, contre 2,25% pour celui de la banque centrale européenne. "Cela ne résoudrait pas les problèmes structurels du pays, mais cela pourrait devenir un catalyseur pour une économie plus saine", a dit Vilhjalmur Hilmarsson, économiste en chef chez Viska, l'un des syndicats les plus importants d'Islande. La cheffe de l'opposition islandaise Gudrun Hafsteinsdottir, qui a mené la campagne du "non", a estimé que la question économique était exagérée. "Ce ne sont pas des problèmes que Bruxelles réglera pour nous. Ce sont des problèmes que les hommes et les femmes politiques islandais doivent résoudre", a-t-elle affirmé. LA PÊCHE, POINT DE CONTENTIEUX L'île, dont les paysages volcaniques ont servi de décor à la série Game of Thrones de HBO, vit de la pêche, de l'aluminium et du tourisme. Les opposants à une adhésion à l'UE affirment que l'Islande bénéficie déjà d'un accès au marché unique européen grâce à l'Espace économique européen, sans les coûts ni les obligations d'une adhésion complète. Ils estiment également qu'obtenir une exemption permanente de Bruxelles sur la pêche serait difficile. "Je sais que l'Union européenne promettra de la souplesse, surtout au début, mais nous savons que cela ne s'inscrira pas dans la durée", a dit Gudrun Hafsteinsdottir. Les bureaux de vote ouvriront leurs portes à 09h00 GMT et fermeront à 22h00. VOIR AUSSI: LE POINT sur le référendum en Islande sur les négociations d'adhésion à l'UE. ([USN:L8N44P0SC TEXT:"Full Story"])

item.title: Judge deals blow to Trump moves to deport pro-Palestinian activists
item.description: A federal judge on Friday ruled that laws that President Donald Trump's administration used to cancel visas and initiate deportation proceedings against noncitizen college students based on their pro-Palestinian advocacy and criticism of Israel are unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Friday ruled that laws that President Donald Trump's administration used to cancel visas and initiate deportation proceedings against noncitizen college students based on their pro-Palestinian advocacy and criticism of Israel are unconstitutional. U.S. District Judge Noel Wise in San Jose, California in a blistering ruling chastised the U.S. State Department and U.S. Department of Homeland Security for how they had deployed provisions of federal immigration law to target non-citizens for deportation for expressing views they wanted to suppress. The judge, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden, said that in the United States, free speech, including the freedom to criticize the government and its leaders, was evidence of the strength of the country's democracy. "That strength is diminished when members of our society – citizens and noncitizens alike – must self-censor and 'behave' or suffer the government’s retaliation," she said. The State Department and DHS did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Wise's ruling focused on how the Trump administration, from March 2025, began revoking visas and detaining non-citizens who engaged in pro-Palestinian advocacy on campus, starting with the arrest of Columbia University graduate Mahmoud Khalil, who is [USN:L1N41Z0RU TEXT:"fighting separately"] to avoid being deported. Those arrests formed the basis of a lawsuit that was filed in August 2025 by Stanford University’s student newspaper, The Stanford Daily, which alleged that some of its writers with student visas had refrained from covering pro-Palestinian student protests and topics related to the Middle East conflict as a result of the administration's policies. The newspaper's lawyers argued that two provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act that the administration relied upon to cancel student visas and initiate deportation proceedings violated the U.S. Constitution's First and Fifth Amendments as applied to constitutionally protected speech. Those laws allowed Secretary of State Marco Rubio to render noncitizens deportable if he personally determined someone's action “compromises a compelling foreign policy interest" and allowed him to revoke someone's visa at his discretion. Wise agreed with the newspaper, saying that when a noncitizen's speech is the reason behind a visa revocation and deportation determination, "the government is singling out that speech for disfavored treatment based on its viewpoint or content." Conor Fitzpatrick, whose group Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression represented the student newspaper, in a statement said the ruling "proves that free speech isn’t a privilege, but the inalienable right of every man, woman, and child." The ruling was similar to a [USN:L2N3VH0RP TEXT:"decision last year"] by Boston-based U.S. District Judge William Young, who similarly found the administration had acted unconstitutionally by adopting a policy of revoking visas, arresting, detaining and deporting foreign students and faculty engaged in pro-Palestinian advocacy. Wise in her ruling expressed concern the administration had moved on to target people for expressing other types of views it disfavored, saying eventually the "targets may include anyone in the United States who exercises their freedom of speech to simply express opinions the government does not like." "This downward spiral is antithetical to our Constitution that recognizes our right to speak freely," she wrote. "Here you can simultaneously hate the content of a person’s speech and love the country that cherishes the freedom to allow it."

item.title: Logan Henderson tosses gem as Brewers shut down Rangers
item.description: Logan Henderson was nearly perfect for the Milwaukee Brewers, who won their third straight game, beating the visiting Texas Rangers 6-1 on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Logan Henderson was nearly perfect for the Milwaukee Brewers, who won their third straight game, beating the visiting Texas Rangers 6-1 on Friday night. Henderson (9-2) faced 22 batters over seven innings, with Danny Jansen's two-out home run in the third inning the only blemish on his stat line. The 24-year-old rookie right-hander struck out seven as he tied his major league high in innings pitched and continued a dominant stretch since the All-Star break (6-1, 1.88 ERA). William Contreras drove in three while going 2-for-4, and Jake Bauers went 2-for-2 with three walks and scored twice for the team with the best record in the major leagues. Christian Yelich (3-for-5) enjoyed his sixth three-hit game of the season to lead the 14-hit attack. Milwaukee gave Henderson the lead early. Brice Turang led off the bottom of the first with a bunt single off Rangers starter Cody Bradford (0-3) and reached second thanks to Bradford's throwing error. The Brewers second baseman advanced to third on Jackson Chourio's deep flyout to right field and scored on a Contreras groundout. Yelich followed with a double to make it 2-0, scoring Bauers. Bradford settled down from there, but the Brewers got to him one last time in the sixth when David Hamilton's two-out single to center field scored Garrett Mitchell from second. Just before Hamilton got to the plate, Rangers manager Skip Schumaker visited the mound, and reliever Tyler Alexander left the bullpen thinking he was coming in. Instead, he would enter a batter later. Bradford, in his fifth start since returning from a left elbow injury sustained in 2025 spring training, threw 100 pitches, 19 more than in any of his other appearances this season. He allowed three runs on nine hits and two walks with no strikeouts. Aaron Ashby relieved Henderson in the eighth inning, allowing a single and a walk to bring up the tying run in Jansen. However, the Rangers catcher grounded out to Turang to end the threat. DL Hall struck out the side in a perfect ninth as Texas lost its third straight game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hunter Brown fans 10 as Astros beat Mets
item.description: Hunter Brown struck out a season-high 10 over 6 2/3 solid innings Friday night as the visiting Houston Astros beat the New York Mets 3-1 in the opener of a three-game interleague series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Hunter Brown struck out a season-high 10 over 6 2/3 solid innings Friday night as the visiting Houston Astros beat the New York Mets 3-1 in the opener of a three-game interleague series. Daulton Varsho had the go-ahead two-run single in the sixth for the Astros, who opened a two-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the American League West. Yainer Diaz added an RBI single two batters later as Houston improved to 3-1 since the exit of general manager Dana Brown. Carson Benge laced an RBI double for the Mets, who have lost three straight -- their longest losing streak since a three-game skid from July 31-Aug. 2. Hunter Brown (4-3) allowed one run on five hits and one walk while authoring the longest start by an Astros pitcher since Aug. 10, when Hayden Wesneski lasted seven innings against the San Francisco Giants. The 10 strikeouts were the most for Brown since June 14, 2025, when he whiffed 12 batters against the Minnesota Twins. Brown exited his latest start after allowing a single to Marcus Semien, but Bryan Abreu struck out Brett Baty to escape the jam. Abreu threw a perfect eighth and Josh Hader notched his 20th save with a 1-2-3 ninth. Jeremy Pena and Jose Altuve had the Astros' other hits. Pena added a stolen base. New York starter Christian Scott (4-4) gave up the three runs on one hit and five walks while striking out two over 5 1/3 innings. The five walks tied a career high for Scott, who also walked five in his season debut against the Twins on April 23. Scott opened the sixth by fanning Pena before he walked the bases loaded. Nate Lavender entered and surrendered the hits to Varsho and Diaz. Semien had two hits and a walk in three plate appearances. Francisco Lindor and Luis Torrens had the Mets' other hits. Lindor scored New York's run on Benge's fourth-inning double. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cam Schlittler, Yankees hold on to blank Red Sox
item.description: Cam Schlittler withstood five walks in 5 2/3 innings and Yankees outfielders started a pair of double plays during New York's 1-0 victory over the visiting Boston Red Sox on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cam Schlittler withstood five walks in 5 2/3 innings and Yankees outfielders started a pair of double plays during New York's 1-0 victory over the visiting Boston Red Sox on Friday night. Paul Goldschmidt homered off Boston starter Patrick Sandoval (1-3) in the third inning, helping the Yankees move three games ahead of Boston for the American League's top wild-card spot. Schlittler (12-6) tied a career high with the five walks. He allowed two hits, struck out eight, and lowered his AL-leading ERA to 2.09. He allowed a double to Wilyer Abreu with two outs in the third, then struck out Willson Contreras. Schlittler also surpassed 200 strikeouts for the season, the first time he has reached that mark. He allowed a single to Ceddanne Rafaela in the fifth, but the game stayed scoreless thanks to teammate Trent Grisham. The New York center fielder caught Abreu's line drive, then threw to Jazz Chisholm Jr., and the second baseman's throw to Goldschmidt at first doubled off Rafaela. With one out in the seventh, the Red Sox had runners on second and third against Paul Blackburn. Contreras hit a fly ball to left field. Cody Bellinger moved in a few steps and made a perfect one-hop throw to catcher Austin Wells, who tagged out Rafaela as the runner fell to the dirt. Goldschmidt gave the Yankees the lead with his first homer since July 24 when he hit Sandoval's first-pitch sinker into the left field bleachers. Schlittler exited after walking Caleb Durbin with two outs in the sixth, and the Red Sox deployed three right-handed pinch hitters against lefty Brent Headrick. Jahmai Jones walked and Eli White hit a slow infield single to load the bases. After Headrick fell behind Andruw Monasterio and reached a full count, the inning ended with a fly ball to right fielder Heliot Ramos. In the bottom of the inning, New York loaded the bases with a single by Ben Rice and consecutive one-out walks by Ramos and Grisham. Sandoval then was replaced by Greg Weissert, who kept it a one-run game by getting George Lombard Jr. to line and before fanning Chisholm with a high fastball. After Bellinger's sixth outfield assist ended the seventh, Blackburn pitched a perfect eighth and David Bednar recorded a 1-2-3 ninth for his 31st save. Sandoval allowed one run on three hits over 5 1/3 innings. He struck out seven and walked four. The Red Sox fell to 9-10 since a 32-5 run that included a four-game sweep of the Yankees in Boston and a 15-game winning streak. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nepal resumes flood rescue, seeks technical help and billions of dollars
item.description: Nearly 3,000 people remain missing, including about 2,426 in Nepal and 554 in Tibet's Gyirong County, among them at least 540 foreign nationals, many of them Hindu pilgrims from India.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma, Saurabh Sharma, Sahana Bajracharya, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: Nepal resumed search and rescue work on Saturday after a brief weather-related suspension as authorities searched for nearly 3,000 missing people following a devastating flood that killed hundreds and tore through a region bordering Tibet. The impoverished Himalayan nation of 30 million people called for specialist foreign assistance and its finance minister told Reuters it would also need about $4 billion to $5 billion to rebuild after the disaster. Triggered by a [USN:L1N44O06X TEXT:"glacier collapse"], a torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris hurtled through [USN:L6N44N0BL TEXT:"mountain"] river systems on Wednesday, killing at least 669 people in Nepal and seven in China's Tibet and sweeping away buildings, bridges and power stations. Nearly 3,000 people remain missing, including about 2,426 in Nepal and 554 in Tibet's Gyirong County, among them at least [USN:L1N44O0KX TEXT:"540 foreign nationals,"] many of them Hindu pilgrims from India. DECOMPOSED, UNRECOGNISABLE BODIES TO BE BURIED Search and rescue operations were temporarily halted because of rain and fog but resumed later in the afternoon, a police officer in hard-hit Rasuwa district said. "Helicopters are flying and the operation resumed following some improvement in weather," he said, on condition of anonymity as he is not authorised to speak to the media. Authorities [USN:L6N44P04B TEXT:"had also suspended"] rescue work on Friday when a lake, formed across the Nepal-China border after the flood, began overflowing into Nepal's Lhende Khola and Trishuli rivers. By Saturday, the [USN:L4N44Q013 TEXT:"risk"] had eased and parts of the lake bed were visible, Chinese authorities and state broadcaster CCTV said. Satellite images suggested water was slowly draining from the lake, gradually reducing its size, CCTV reported. The lake is one of two upstream of the flood zone being monitored by Nepal. [USN:L6N44P0OC TEXT:"Flood risks will persist"] until both have fully drained, an official warned. Three days after the disaster, authorities said some bodies being recovered had decomposed beyond recognition. They would be buried after legal formalities because of health risks and a fear of disease outbreaks. "DNA samples will be collected, and the bodies will be buried in an open space," the Chitwan district administration said in a notice. FAMILIES SEARCH FOR THE MISSING In Kathmandu, families of missing people gathered outside Maharajgunj Medical Campus, where some bodies had been taken. Many tried to identify relatives from photographs of the bodies displayed on gates and boundary walls. In Malaysia, families of 91 citizens listed as "uncontactable" across Tibet and Nepal also waited for news. Manivannan Rethinam, a representative for some of them, urged the foreign ministry to establish a communication channel for faster updates, saying the lack of information was "profoundly painful" for relatives awaiting news. Malaysia's foreign ministry said search and rescue and verification efforts were continuing. For survivors, the ordeal is far from over as they face the task of rebuilding their lives. Saraswati Ghale, 43, said her home was destroyed in the flood. She recalled scrambling uphill as the water struck, shaking the ground "like there was an earthquake". "I don’t have anything (left) ... I am saved but who knows how things will pan out," she said. Nepal's Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters the government's initial estimate was that rebuilding would cost between $4 billion and $5 billion. "This is just an estimate. Loss and damage is being assessed," he said. TECHNICAL AID HEADS TO NEPAL Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said the country did not need help with search and rescue but [USN:L6N44Q00H TEXT:"required specialist assistance"] to rescue people trapped in tunnels, restore transport and communication lines where bridges had been destroyed, identify bodies, conduct DNA testing and store bodies for longer periods. "We have already made requests for such specialised services and technical assistance in areas where we don't have enough expertise and technical know-how," he told Reuters late on Friday. A team of Indian tunnel experts arrived in Nepal on Saturday, he said, while China's Xinhua news agency reported Beijing had [USN:P8N43G01Z TEXT:"dispatched five tunnel experts"] to support rescue efforts, with four more due to join them. India has already sent three flights carrying 60 tons of relief supplies, including blankets, medicines, and food. It has also offered disaster-response personnel, prefabricated bridges and technical teams to help restore connectivity, the foreign ministry said. Chinese authorities are also racing to trace more than 500 people still missing after the flood. Rescuers reached the worst-hit Gyirong border crossing complex on Friday, using ropes to navigate forests and cliffs after roads leading to the site were destroyed. In bleak, rainy conditions on Saturday morning, more than 50 rescue workers combed through the rubble of boulders and mud, looking for signs of life and calling out for survivors, CCTV reported. Surveillance footage from the crossing showed torrents of water and debris engulfing buildings when the flood hit, as people tried to flee.

item.title: George Springer's 4-hit performance powers Blue Jays past Mariners
item.description: George Springer went 4-for-4 with a solo homer Friday night as the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the visiting Seattle Mariners 8-1.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: George Springer went 4-for-4 with a solo homer Friday night as the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the visiting Seattle Mariners 8-1. Nathan Lukes and Kazuma Okamoto added solo shots for the Blue Jays in the opener of a three-game series. Okamoto had three RBIs. Dylan Cease (9-5) allowed one run, four hits and one walk while striking out eight in six innings as Toronto earned just its second win in five games. Dominic Canzone stroked a solo homer for the Mariners while going 2-for-4. Randy Arozarena had a single and two walks as the Mariners dropped the opener of a six-game road trip. Seattle has lost two in a row. The Mariners took an early lead when Canzone clubbed a 1-1 fastball 433 feet to right-center with one out in the first inning. Toronto answered with three runs against Emerson Hancock (7-8) in the bottom of the first. Brett Bateman led off with a single, stole second and took third when Lukes grounded out to the pitcher. Hancock favored his leg after making the tag on the first base line but continued after being checked by a trainer. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. grounded an RBI double past third base that bounced off the barrier in front of the stands. Springer beat out an infield hit to shortstop with Guerrero taking third on the throwing error. After Jesus Sanchez was hit by a pitch to load the bases, Okamoto hit a sacrifice fly to the wall in right and Andres Gimenez grounded an RBI single up the middle. Lukes homered to right on a 1-1 changeup with one out in the fifth. Two batters later, Springer clobbered a second-deck shot to left on a 1-2 sweeper, giving Toronto a 5-1 lead. Hancock allowed five runs, eight hits and no walks with one strikeout in five innings. Cease worked around two singles in the sixth inning before departing. Okamoto led off the bottom of the sixth with a homer to left against Seranthony Dominguez on a 2-2 sweeper. The Blue Jays added two runs in the seventh against Michael Rucker. Lukes walked, Springer singled with one out and Myles Straw grounded an RBI single to center. Another run scored on Okamoto's single. CJ Van Eyk, recalled by Toronto on Friday from Triple-A Buffalo, pitched around a ninth-inning walk. Simeon Woods Richardson was designated for assignment. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rays ride 5-run fourth to pull away from Padres
item.description: Tampa Bay's Yandy Diaz went 2-for-5 with a home run and two RBIs, and the American League East-leading Rays produced a five-run fourth inning Friday night to breeze past the San Diego Padres 9-4 in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tampa Bay's Yandy Diaz went 2-for-5 with a home run and two RBIs, and the American League East-leading Rays produced a five-run fourth inning Friday night to breeze past the San Diego Padres 9-4 in St. Petersburg, Fla. The Rays, who were 2-5 on their previous homestand, became the first AL squad to reach 80 wins. Chandler Simpson went 2-for-4 with a double, two runs and two stolen bases. Taylor Walls had two hits, two runs and a stolen base. Cedric Mullins homered, scored twice and drove in two runs. Starting pitcher Shane McClanahan (10-6) earned his fourth win in eight starts, pitching 5 2/3 innings and allowing four runs (three earned) on three hits. He struck out four and walked two. San Diego's Jackson Merrill went 2-for-3, stroked a two-run homer, walked, and scored twice, accounting for half of his team's hits. Starter Casey Mize (5-8) surrendered seven runs (two earned) on six hits over five innings, with a walk and a strikeout. In Tampa Bay's first matchup with San Diego in Florida in nearly two years, Diaz drilled a 2-1 sinker up in the zone from Mize down the right field line for a solo homer, his 20th, in the third. The deep ball was the leadoff hitter's 120th of his career and 119th with the Rays, moving him past B.J. Upton into fifth place in franchise history. Mize helped fuel the rally when he threw away a potential double-play comebacker, firing wildly wide of second and putting runners on the corners. The Rays scored five runs with just two hits via Mullins' fielder's choice that did not result in an out, a wild pitch, Jorge Mateo's sacrifice fly, and run-scoring singles from Walls and Diaz for a 6-0 advantage. Aided by second baseman Mateo's error, the Padres answered with RBI fielder's choices by Freddy Fermin and Jake Cronenworth to cut it to 6-2. Jonny DeLuca increased the lead to five by singling in Simpson in the fifth, but Merrill's 22nd blast to right-center in the next frame made it 7-4. Junior Caminero looped a broken-bat RBI single in the sixth, and Mullins homered to right off Wandy Peralta in the following inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: War weighs on Iran's economy as US intensifies sanctions
item.description: Tehran signaled no retreat as they acknowledged the war's economic toll.
item.dc:creator: Eman Abouhassira, Yasmine Ghania, Ahmed Tolba
item.content:encoded: Iranian leaders are acknowledging the economic toll of war with the U.S., with the supreme leader urging the government to address the hardship and the president saying foreign trade has shrunk by a third due to the American sanctions and blockade. Yet Tehran signalled no retreat on Saturday, vowing to withstand U.S. pressure, pursue diplomacy and maintain what it said was control over the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway giving Iran leverage through its ability to disrupt global energy markets. The government said in a statement on state media that addressing economic pressures caused by sanctions and war was a central focus, including curbing inflation, managing markets, creating jobs, directing investment towards domestic production and gradually reducing dependence on the dollar. Six months after the U.S. and Israel launched the war, negotiations are at an impasse and President Donald Trump's administration has stepped up efforts to punish Iran financially with what it has billed as an "economic D-Day". SANCTIONS COMPOUND TOLL ON IRAN'S ECONOMY Washington has [USN:L1N44L0FC TEXT:"warned countries"] to cut business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions, though the Treasury Department stopped short of imposing penalties against major Iranian trade partners such as China and India, which could have repercussions for the U.S. and global economies. The Treasury imposed sanctions on [USN:L1N44P0N7 TEXT:"Egypt's Banque Misr"] for doing business with Tehran, proposing a rule that would cut off the bank's branches in the United Arab Emirates from dollar transactions. Egypt's central bank said it and the foreign ministry were in contact with U.S. officials concerning the matter, adding the measure was limited to Banque Misr UAE’s U.S. dollar transactions with correspondent banks only. Banque Misr said later in a statement it was reviewing the U.S. Treasury notice, adding that its branch in the UAE continued to provide banking services to its customers in line with applicable rules and procedures. The U.S. also issued sanctions targeting an entity based in Hong Kong and a person linked to Iran's Bank Melli, according to a notice on the Treasury website. The sanctions drive compounds the toll of the war on [USN:L1N44F051 TEXT:"Iran's economy,"] where annual inflation hit 66% last month. Supreme Leader Ayatollah [USN:L6N44N0V3 TEXT:"Mojtaba Khamenei"] — who has not been seen publicly since he was injured in the initial February 28 attack that killed his father and former supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei — called on the government to tackle the economic hardship. "There is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services," according to a written statement attributed to Khamenei. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that Iranian exports and imports had slumped nearly 35% because of U.S. sanctions and a naval blockade of Iranian ports. But he said Iran was able to sell about 90 million barrels of oil during the short-lived memorandum of understanding that the U.S. and Iran signed in June, when Washington permitted Iranian oil sales. IRAN VOWS TO PURSUE DIPLOMACY AND DEFENCE With the U.S. focused on its economic pressure campaign, others have sought to revive diplomatic efforts to end the war. Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met with Iranian leaders in Tehran on Thursday. He said he had stressed during the meeting the importance of returning to the pre-war status of open shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Friday described the talks with Al Thani as "creative". In Saturday's statement, Iran said diplomacy and defence were "two complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings" for protecting the country's national interests, security and territorial integrity. It said it would pursue both tracks in a balanced manner. Qatar, a U.S. ally and Gulf neighbour to Iran, and Pakistan helped broker the June memorandum of understanding that led to a brief ceasefire before disagreements over the vital strait caused it to unravel. Before the war, the waterway carried 20% of the world's oil and LNG. U.S. military commanders say American forces have cleared sea mines from the strait that had been laid months ago by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Trump has repeatedly said the Strait of Hormuz is open, but the Revolutionary Guards' navy said in a statement that such claims "are an obvious lie", reiterating that the waterway remained closed to ships without Iranian permission. Only seven commodity vessels [USN:L1N44P02R TEXT:"transited the strait"] on Thursday, down from 17 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of 15, preliminary shipping data showed on Friday.

item.title: OpenAI to cut off AI models for SpaceX-owned Cursor, escalating feud with Musk
item.description: OpenAI said on Friday that it plans to stop providing AI models to Cursor, the coding-tool company now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, marking a further escalation in the bitter rivalry between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Musk.
item.dc:creator: Anusha Devang Shah, Shubham Kalia
item.content:encoded: OpenAI said on Friday that it plans to stop providing AI models to Cursor, the coding-tool company now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, marking a further escalation in the bitter rivalry between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Musk. Musk and Altman have been at odds for years, a feud that culminated earlier this year in a trial over Musk's $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI. During the [USN:L6N41R11A TEXT:"trial"], Musk's lawyer said that Musk and other witnesses had testified that Altman was a liar, while OpenAI argued that Musk had sought control of the company. "We are making this choice because we cannot be confident that SpaceX will use our technology within our terms of service, based on our experience with Elon Musk's companies violating contracts," OpenAI said in a blog post. Musk responded early on Saturday in an X post, writing, "I couldn't care less." He accused Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman of being "untrustworthy," while repeating his assertion that they "stole an open source nonprofit." Musk, the world's richest person, had sued OpenAI and Altman for "stealing a charity" by betraying the company's original nonprofit mission for their own enrichment. A federal jury ruled against Musk earlier this year, finding that he had filed the case too late. However, Michael Truell, a co-founder of Cursor and now an executive at SpaceX, said on X that the company was speaking with the OpenAI team to resolve this issue. Hours after OpenAI's announcement, Anthropic, which rivals both firms but has an [USN:L6N41X1FW TEXT:"ongoing"] partnership with SpaceX, said it planned to increase compute to support Claude models in Cursor, according to Tom Brown, one of the co-founders of the firm. In its blog post, OpenAI said that X, formerly known as Twitter and now part of SpaceX, had breached the terms of its contract with OpenAI after Musk acquired the platform. "To work with a large partner like SpaceX, we typically rely on custom contracts to ensure compliance with our terms of service and that the integration provides for safety at scale," the AI company added. The ChatGPT-maker said it proposed a shutoff date of November 12, 2026, adding that its agreement with Cursor gave it a limited time window to cancel the contract following "a change of control." SpaceX (SPCX.O) [USN:L4N42O0W5 TEXT:"announced"] a deal to buy Anysphere, the startup behind Cursor, for $60 billion in an all-stock deal in June, and completed the acquisition earlier this month.

item.title: Michael Wacha fans 10 in 8 innings as Royals blank Guardians
item.description: All-Star Michael Wacha struck out 10 over eight innings and Carter Jensen hit a two-run homer in the ninth, sending the red-hot Kansas City Royals to a 3-0 victory over the host Cleveland Guardians on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: All-Star Michael Wacha struck out 10 over eight innings and Carter Jensen hit a two-run homer in the ninth, sending the red-hot Kansas City Royals to a 3-0 victory over the host Cleveland Guardians on Friday night. Wacha (8-8) allowed four singles and did not issue a walk in tying his longest start of the season. He only permitted one runner to get past first base over 103 pitches. The right-hander powered Kansas City to its 11th win in 12 games since Aug. 16. Steven Cruz loaded the bases in the ninth before earning his sixth save in seven opportunities. The Royals scored their first run in the fifth when Bobby Witt Jr. led off with a double and came home on Salvador Perez's groundout to shortstop. The Guardians had their seven-game winning streak snapped, but remain in the third and final American League wild-card position with 27 contests remaining. They fell 3 1/2 games behind the first-place Chicago White Sox in the AL Central. Cleveland starter Tanner Bibee (5-14) tied Shane Baz of the Baltimore Orioles for the major league lead in losses, giving up one run on seven hits in six innings for his career-high 17th quality start. The right-hander struck out five, walked two and hit a batter. Cruz gave up singles to Chase DeLauter and Jo Adell, and hit Travis Bazzana with a pitch with two outs to send the potential winning run to the plate for the Guardians. Rookie Angel Genao pinch-hit, but hit a weak grounder back to the mound to end the game. Jensen went deep against Craig Yoho in the ninth, plating Tyler Tolbert. Witt has reached base safely in 22 of 23 games since returning from the injured list on Aug. 4. The Royals had loaded the bases with two outs in the third, but Bibee retired Nick Loftin on a short fly to center to keep the game scoreless. Jac Caglianone had two hits in the first three innings after banging out five Thursday at the Toronto Blue Jays. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jackson Kent fires 7 strong innings for first win as Nats rout Marlins
item.description: Brady House smacked a three-run homer, Jackson Kent pitched seven innings of one-run ball to earn his first major league win and the Washington Nationals beat the visiting Miami Marlins 9-2 on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
